title: NTLMSSP: Add NT Credentials UAT for multiple passwords and hashes
description:
Replace the single NT Password string preference with a UAT that
allows configuring multiple credentials. Each entry can be either
an NT Password (plaintext) or an NT Hash (32 hex chars).

This enables decryption of NTLM-authenticated traffic when only the
NT hash is available (e.g., from secretsdump), without requiring the
original plaintext password. Multiple credentials are tried in order
until a matching one is found.

Tested with NTLMSSP-authenticated SMB3 traffic.

AI-Assisted: yes (Claude)

notes.body: Minimally this preference needs to be marked as obsolete and an "upgrade path" needs to be created so that if an existing preference file has a password, it is upgraded to be included in the new UAT.

Sorry but could you kindly point me in the right direction on how to implement the "upgrade path"? IIUC, `prefs_register_obsolete_preference` marks the preference as obsolete, which means Wireshark will silently ignore it when reading preference files. So we can't both mark it obsolete and read its value.
Should an effort be made to encrypt the passwords provided so they aren't stored in a plain text file (now that we're upgrading the feature)?

Thanks for the review! Good point! I (and Claude :P) looked into this, but it seems that Wireshark currently has no credential encryption infrastructure. All existing dissectors store secrets in plaintext UAT/preference files:

- SNMP (packet-snmp.c): auth/priv passwords stored as plaintext UAT_FLD_LSTRING
- TLS (packet-tls.c): PKCS#12 key passwords stored as plaintext UAT_FLD_CSTRING
- IEEE 802.11 (packet-ieee80211.c): WEP/WPA keys stored as plaintext UAT_CSTRING_CB_DEF

There is no UAT_FLD_PASSWORD type, no OS keyring integration (DPAPI, libsecret, Keychain), and uat_save() writes field values directly via fprintf().

Adding encryption for NTLMSSP alone would be inconsistent with every other dissector. Should this be tracking as a separate feature request? Potentially, we can add an encrypted/password UAT field type or OS credential store integration that benefits all dissectors.
Hi, any chance to get this reviewed or merged? Would appreciate it very much!
